title: Proposed Chartered Institute of media professionals to develop and maintain media standards
byline: The proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals is vested with powers to introduce, develop, maintain and monitor professional standards in the field of media, the Bill to this effect which was tabled in Parliament said.

title: New Animal Welfare Bill: Rs. 250,000 fine, two-year jail for animal cruelty
byline: Those convicted of animal cruelty could face fines of up to Rs. 250,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, under Sri Lanka’s long-awaited Animal Welfare Bill, which has now been published in the Government Gazette.

title: Special arrack price increased by Rs. 20
byline: The price of a 750 ml bottle of special arrack has been increased by Rs. 20, the Sri Lanka Distilleries Company said.

title: Dengue vaccine not the solution to current outbreak: Expert
byline: While saying that the dengue vaccine is not a solution to the current dengue epidemic, Consultant Physician Dr. Ananda Wijewickrama urged the public to seek immediate medical attention if they develop symptoms in order to reduce fatalities.

title: Will the “tax shock” kill the Sri Lankan economy?
byline: Under the latest IMF extended fund facility program, Sri Lanka has achieved substantial increase in tax revenue – to a level never seen in the history. Data show that for the first quarter of 2026, tax collections increased by an impressive 49 percent compared to same period last year. With GDP growing at 5.1 percent, and inflation below 2.5 percent, first quarter economic performance looks good on “IMF report card!”

title: El Nino to trigger unpredictable rainfall later this year, steps taken for food security
byline: With the development of El Niño conditions altering weather patterns in Sri Lanka, the government is planning for advancing the Maha cultivation season in a bid to avert any impact on food security, a Minister said yesterday.

title: Japan seeks interest on delayed LRT compensation payments
byline: Japan has requested the Sri Lankan government to pay interest on the delayed settlement of compensation arising from the cancellation of the Japan-funded Light Rail Transit (LRT) project, in addition to the compensation already paid in three installments during 2024, Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Ratnayake told Parliament yesterday.

title: US signs landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
byline: The US and Saudi Arabia have signed a landmark deal that will reportedly allow the Gulf kingdom to develop a civilian nuclear programme.

title: Navy seizes Indian fishing trawler with nine fishermen for poaching in SL waters
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy seized an Indian fishing trawler and apprehended nine Indian fishermen during a special search operation conducted today after they were found engaging in poaching in Sri Lankan waters off Mannar, having crossed the International Maritime Boundary Line (IMBL).

title: Gun discovered after clash between Chinese nationals at Port City
byline: A pistol and a communication device have been found in a vehicle linked to a clash between two groups of Chinese nationals at the Colombo Port City, police said.

title: Five soldiers killed in southern Thailand checkpoint attack
byline: Five Thai paramilitary soldiers have been killed and six civilians wounded in an attack on a security checkpoint in the country’s rebel-hit south, according to the army.

title: Vehicle imports drop remarkably: Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Finance Anil Jayantha Fernando said today that vehicle imports have reduced remarkably after the imposition of the 50 percent surcharge on vehicle imports.

title: CAA warns private hospitals against overcharging for FBC, Dengue tests
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has reminded private hospitals and laboratories that maximum charges remain in force for certain medical laboratory tests, following reports that a private hospital in Jaffna had allegedly charged above the approved fee for a Full Blood Count (FBC) test.

title: Congo says more than 1,000 die of Ebola, confirmed cases rise to 2,536
byline: The number ​of confirmed Ebola ‌cases in the Democratic ​Republic of ​Congo has increased to 2,536, ⁠including ​1,033 deaths, government ​data showed late on Wednesday.

title: Selfie attempt at Knuckles Waterfall claims lives of two schoolboys
byline: Two schoolboys lost their lives after attempting to take selfies from the top of the Jodu Ella waterfall in the Knuckles forest range yesterday.

title: Gotabaya Rajapaksa appears before Court of Appeal over arrest petition
byline: Former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa appeared before the Court of Appeal today (23) to observe proceedings related to a writ petition he has filed seeking an order preventing his arrest and detention.

title: Beware of fake police officers demanding bank details on WhatsApp
byline: The Sri Lanka Police have issued an urgent public warning over a surge in financial scams involving fraudsters impersonating police officers and other government officials to steal money and sensitive banking information.

title: Police Officer’s house targeted in shooting in Beliatta
byline: A house belonging to a police officer in the Walawala area of Beliatta came under gunfire, police said.

title: SC rules activist’s arrest during ‘GotaGoHome’ protests violated Fundamental Rights
byline: The Supreme Court today held that the arrest of social activist Anuruddha Bandara during the 2022 “GotaGoHome” protest movement was arbitrary and unlawful, ruling that the police violated his fundamental rights by arresting him without objectively reasonable grounds.

title: Leader of the House wants MP Archchuna suspended from Parliament
byline: Leader of the House Bimal Ratnayake, who said that MP Ramanathan Archchuna is suffering from a mental illness, wanted him suspended from Parliament as per standing orders.

title: Houthis claim attack on oil tankers as US launches more strikes on Iran
byline: Yemen’s Houthis say they have attacked two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea as the US launched its 12th consecutive night of strikes on Iran.

title: Speaker, MP clash verbally over raising of questions
byline: Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne engaged in a verbal clash with MP Chanaka Madugoda during which the former accused the MP of taking too much time on questions.

title: Court rejects bid to delay A/L examination by two months
byline: The Court of Appeal today dismissed a writ application filed by a group of students seeking to postpone the upcoming G.C.E. Advanced Level examination by two months.

title: Wreckage of Pan Am plane that shaped aviation safety found 74 years on
byline: The wreckage of a Pan American Airways plane has been found 74 years after it plunged into the Atlantic Ocean in a crash that prompted mandatory airline safety briefings.

title: Lanka Premier League: Galle Gallants undone by Dambulla Sixers
byline: Unbeaten Galle Gallants met their Waterloo when they suffered a six-wicket defeat at the hands of Dambulla Sixers in the eighth match of the Lanka Premier League T20 tournament played under floodlights at the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium yesterday.

title: New train service from Colombo Fort to Thalaimannar Port begins tomorrow
byline: Sri Lanka Railways will commence operations of a new train service between Colombo Fort and Thalaimannar Port from tomorrow (July 24).

title: Lanka Sathosa reduces prices of 11 essential food items
byline: Lanka Sathosa has announced a reduction in the prices of 11 essential food items with effect from July 24, 2026.

title: School second term to end on July 24
byline: The second school term for Sinhala and Tamil schools in government schools and government-approved private schools will end on Friday, July 24, 2026, the Education Ministry said.

title: 17 of 28 Negombo Prison deaths caused by gunshot injuries, court told
byline: The Negombo Magistrate’s Court has been informed that 17 of the 28 deaths linked to the incident inside Negombo Prison were caused by gunshot injuries, while the remaining 11 deaths resulted from assaults involving blunt weapons.

title: One injured in shooting near Kuppiyawatta Cemetery in Dematagoda
byline: A person has sustained injuries following a shooting incident that occurred near the Kuppiyawatta cemetery in Dematagoda.

title: Body of abducted Chinese national found in Eheliyagoda
byline: The body of a Chinese national, suspected to have been abducted and murdered by a group of fellow Chinese nationals at the Colombo Port City, has been discovered hidden in a forest area in Karandana, Eheliyagoda.

title: Opposition discusses Supreme Court retirement age proposal
byline: A special discussion among opposition party leaders on the government’s proposal to extend the retirement age of Supreme Court judges is currently being held at the Opposition Leader’s Office in Colombo.

title: Two Chinese nationals arrested at BIA over alleged Port City gang clash killing
byline: Two Chinese nationals accused of killing a member of a rival gang during a clash between two Chinese groups at the Colombo Port City were arrested at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) while attempting to flee the country.

title: Prof. Peiris to establish legal research trust for Colombo University and Law College
byline: Professor G.L. Peiris has announced plans to establish a Trust Fund to support legal research and academic initiatives at the Faculty of Law, University of Colombo, and the Sri Lanka Law College.

title: Labour Department suspends EPF services on July 30 and 31
byline: The Labour Department has announced that public services related to the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) Database and Digital EPF system will be unavailable on July 30 and 31, 2026, due to essential maintenance work on its computer system.

title: Former State Minister’s son remanded over Rs. 20Mn robbery case
byline: Former State Minister Shantha Bandara’s son, Anuda Bandara, was today remanded until July 27 over his alleged involvement in the robbery of Rs. 20 million belonging to a Chinese national.

title: Tax burden unfair despite government revenue claims: Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organizer Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa has accused the government of imposing an unfair tax burden on the public despite claiming to have large amounts of revenue.

title: Port City helipad among key aviation proposals
byline: The Ministry of Defence has reviewed progress on measures to strengthen Sri Lanka’s domestic aviation sector, with discussions including a proposal to establish a dedicated helicopter landing facility within Colombo Port City.

title: Chinese Embassy seeks probe into Port City clash
byline: The Chinese Embassy in Sri Lanka has urged Sri Lankan authorities to conduct a thorough investigation into a violent confrontation involving Chinese nationals at the Colombo Port City and establish the facts as soon as possible.

title: Mid-air 10-person brawl halts easyJet flight
byline: A mid-air brawl involving around 10 passengers forced a Liverpool-bound easyJet plane to fly back to Tenerife, according to air traffic control.

title: Grade 5 Scholarship Examination 2026 to be held on August 9
byline: The Department of Examinations has announced that the Grade 5 Scholarship Examination 2026, conducted to select students for schools and award scholarships, will be held on Sunday, August 9, 2026.

title: Oil prices hit $100 for the first time since May
byline: Oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May as the escalating conflict in the Middle East reignited fears over global energy supplies.

title: Venue and dates for World Test Championship 2027 Final revealed
byline: The Oval in London has been confirmed as the venue for next year’s ICC World Test Championship Final, which will be played from Wednesday, 9 June to Sunday, 13 June.
